title: The Sex Recession Has an Ideological Tilt: Why Liberals Are Having Less Sex in the Digital Age
gist: Maria Baer and Brad Wilcox argue America's 'sex recession' (weekly sex down from 55% in 1990 to 37%) is driven largely by the retreat from marriage, and that the decline within marriage has largely spared religious and conservative couples. They hypothesize that liberals' greater time online, exposure to gender-war content and porn helps explain a gap, especially among wives (45% vs. 55% weekly).

insights.claim: The share of American adults reporting weekly sex has fallen from 55% in 1990 to 37% today, with the retreat from marriage a major reason.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: A macro indicator of declining coupling with implications for fertility and household formation.
insights.quote: the share of adults reporting weekly sex falling from 55% in 1990 to 37% today
insights.locator: Unfortunately, America is on the downslope

insights.claim: Among married couples aged 18-64, weekly sex fell from 59% in 2008 to about 49% today.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Even within marriage intimacy is declining, a signal of broader social disengagement.
insights.locator: But today’s married couples aren’t fully immune

insights.claim: Blanchflower and Oswald found married people have more sex than single, divorced, widowed or separated people, contradicting the pop-culture view that monogamous marriage kills passion.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Marriage decline mechanically deepens the sex recession.
insights.quote: married people have more sex than those who are single, divorced, widowed or separated

insights.claim: Churchgoing and religiously observant couples are having sex about as often as in the 1990s, with almost two-thirds intimate regularly, while fewer than half of secular couples have weekly sex.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Religiosity is a strong differentiator of family and intimacy outcomes.
insights.quote: Churchgoing couples in America are still having sex about as often as they were in the 1990s.

insights.claim: General Social Survey data show marital sex among married women 20-55 has fallen sharply for liberals since the 1990s but not for conservatives; among husbands the liberal-conservative gap is not statistically significant.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: The sex recession is partly an ideologically sorted phenomenon.
insights.locator: Data from the General Social Survey

insights.claim: In the 2022 State of Our Unions Survey of about 2,000 married people by YouGov, 55% of conservative wives report weekly sex versus 45% of liberal wives.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Quantifies the ideological gap among wives.
insights.quote: a majority (55%) of conservative wives have sex weekly or more, compared to only a minority (45%) of liberal wives

insights.claim: The authors say the conservative-liberal gap among wives is largely explained by conservatives being more religious, with ideology, social lives and algorithms as possible additional factors.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Religiosity, not politics per se, appears to be the primary driver.
insights.locator: The data suggests that the gap

insights.claim: Survey Center on American Life data show Democratic women are about twice as likely to blame men for challenges women face, and anti-male attitudes surged among left-leaning women since the rise of social media.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Social media appears to amplify gender polarization that weighs on relationship formation.
insights.locator: Liberals are more exposed to messaging

insights.claim: The authors hypothesize that liberals spend more time on social media and so encounter more polarizing 'gender wars' content, which keeps people scrolling but is poison for real relationships.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Engagement-optimized platform content may carry social costs relevant to regulation and platform-risk narratives.
insights.quote: may keep people scrolling. But they can be poison for real relationships.

insights.claim: Researchers found 'lifestyle polarization' among college students: conservatives spend leisure with people at parties, bars, fraternities or church, while liberals are more likely at home or on social media.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Screen time is displacing in-person socializing for a segment of young adults.

insights.claim: Democrats are much more likely than Republicans to say they view porn regularly and nearly twice as likely to call it morally acceptable, per a YouGov survey; porn use is linked to lower marital satisfaction and higher infidelity and divorce.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Online adult content is framed as a corrosive force on marital intimacy.

insights.claim: Democrats are less likely to view marriage as a vehicle for happiness or as important for children, and left-leaning Americans are less likely to be happily married.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Attitudinal divergence on marriage may translate into divergent family formation by ideology.

insights.claim: Blanchflower and Oswald found sexual activity enters strongly positively into happiness equations and the happiness-maximizing number of sexual partners in a year is one.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Supports monogamous marriage as a well-being driver.
insights.locator: Is it, though? Research says the opposite.

insights.claim: Per the General Social Survey, married men 20-55 with regular sex are almost four times more likely to be very happy than unmarried peers with little sex, and comparable married women are three times as likely.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Large well-being gaps tied to marriage and intimacy.
insights.locator: Men who have regular sex and are married

insights.claim: The authors push back on the Call Her Daddy message from Alex Cooper and Sophia Bush that women can always do better than their husbands, arguing research says the opposite.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Highlights the cultural influence of popular podcasts on marriage norms.

insights.claim: The authors' hypothesis is that conservative married couples place a higher premium on intimate time and are more embedded in social networks, especially religious ones, that sustain their marriages.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Community embeddedness may be a key protective factor for family stability.
insights.locator: But in general, conservatism and religiosity

insights.claim: Couples of any ideology seeking greater intimacy should limit time online and prioritize real-world relationships.
insights.speaker: https://www.facebook.com/familystudies/
insights.so_what: Adds to growing cultural pressure against screen time, a headwind narrative for social platforms.
insights.locator: If there is one clear line in the sand
